name: Letting people upload files
summary: Uploads that go straight to storage rather than through your app, with limits on what and how big.

provenance.source: SimpleHire — its S3 storage service, in particular presigned uploads and the key sanitising that keeps a filename from becoming a path
provenance.changes: Reduced to upload and download, scoped every key to an organisation, and pulled the validation out into pure functions so the dangerous parts are testable without a bucket.

env.name: S3_BUCKET
env.description: The bucket your files go in.

env.name: S3_ENDPOINT
env.description: The storage address. Cloudflare R2 and others need this; plain AWS does not.

env.name: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
env.description: The key that lets your app write to the bucket.

env.name: S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
env.description: The other half of that key.

extensionPoints.description: Which file types your product accepts.

postInstall: Create a bucket with your storage provider and put its keys in .env.
Make sure the bucket is private. Presigned links are what give access; a public bucket makes them pointless.
Upload one file and download it again before you rely on this.
limitations: Not run against a live bucket here. The key handling and the limits are tested; the round trip is not.
No virus scanning. If strangers can upload, you need that as well.
solves: attach a file to a record
